teaser.text: BlackRock is an investment manager: it looks after other people’s money and sells institutions the software and data to run portfolios. The dollar usually enters as a fee on assets or a technology contract, then leaves through staff, distribution, fund, and operating costs before the remainder becomes profit.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for BlackRock?

paragraphs.text: The bear case gives earnings of $7,975 million in 2027 and $8,100 million in 2028, reaching $8,505 million in 2029. It reflects weaker markets, lower-fee products and persistent acquisition costs. The bull case reaches $10,560 million, $11,880 million and $13,260 million as higher-fee inflows, cross-selling and private-market growth outpace costs. Technology ACV grew 16% organically in 2025, supporting that upside but not proving it.

The bull case requires broad inflows, successful Aladdin, eFront and Preqin cross-selling, and private-market commitments converting into fee-paying assets. If recurring revenue grows faster than costs, buybacks and multiple expansion reinforce the result. The path reaches $1,706.40 first and $2,339.51 last. Its probability is 20% because several unproven conditions must hold together.

blocks.heading: How much does BlackRock pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise from $24.30 per share to $26.24 and $28.34 in the base case. That is slower than the latest 10% increase, but consistent with annual dividends rising every year from 2021 through 2025. The bear case uses $23.78, $24.97 and $26.22, while the bull case uses $24.64, $27.10 and $29.81. The bear case assumes slower increases rather than a cut because the dividend rose during the 2022 revenue decline.

blocks.heading: Is BlackRock's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is the cash left after operating needs and capital spending. It can fund acquisitions, debt repayment, dividends and buybacks. BlackRock’s shareholder payments exceeded its free cash flow over the five-year period, and in 2025 alone payments reached 115.9% of free cash flow. That left less internally generated cash for expansion.

In 2025, operations produced $3,927 million of cash. Capital spending was $375 million, leaving free cash flow of $3,552 million. That was down from $4,701 million in 2024 and represented 14.7% of revenue.

Stock compensation was $1,307 million. Deducting it from free cash flow produces “real free cash flow” of $2,245 million. The deduction recognises the economic cost to shareholders, even though the company did not make another cash payment in the period.

paragraphs.text: Management targets more than $35 billion of revenue by 2030. It targets at least $15 billion of adjusted operating income. Private markets and technology should provide at least 30% of revenue, supported by at least 5% organic base-fee growth and low-to-mid-teens technology ACV growth. For 2026, guidance calls for $2,000 million of repurchases, including $550 million for the quarter to December 2026.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in BlackRock's next results?

paragraphs.text: The quarter ending December 31, 2026 is the next operating checkpoint. Investors should watch the planned $550 million repurchase alongside the cost outlook. Completing the purchase would show available capital and management confidence; completing it while recurring fees grow faster than expenses would show stronger underlying progress.
